meta.title: Seasons Around the World — Vocabulary Set 2
meta.subject: English Vocabulary
meta.description: Vocabulary practice focusing on Week 13 words: snow, die, hibernate, Northern, Southern, North Pole, dark, appear.

questions.question: What is the soft, white frozen water that falls from clouds in winter?
questions.explanation: Snow is frozen rain that falls as soft white flakes during cold winter weather.

questions.question: To 'die' means to start growing and living.
questions.explanation: False. To 'die' means to stop living or stop growing.

questions.question: Which word is the opposite of 'dark'?
questions.explanation: 'Bright' means filled with light, which is the opposite of 'dark' (having no light).

questions.question: 'Northern' describes the top part of the Earth above the equator.
questions.explanation: True. The Northern part of the world refers to everything north of the equator.

questions.question: Where does the sun never shine in winter, leaving it dark all day?
questions.explanation: The North Pole is at the very top of Earth, and in winter it points away from the sun, so it is dark all day.

questions.question: Bears and some other animals _______ in winter to sleep through the cold months.
questions.hint: To go into a deep winter sleep.
questions.explanation: To hibernate is to spend the winter sleeping or resting in a deep sleep.

questions.question: What does the verb 'appear' mean when flowers 'appear' in spring?
options: To come into sight and be seen
To stay hidden under the snow
questions.explanation: To 'appear' means to become visible or come into sight.

questions.question: Sort these Week 13 words into Actions/States or Places/Things:
questions.explanation: 'Die,' 'hibernate,' and 'appear' are verbs (actions/states). 'Snow' and 'North Pole' are nouns (places/things).

questions.question: 'Southern' refers to the bottom part of the Earth below the equator.
questions.explanation: True. The Southern part refers to the region south of the equator, like Australia or Antarctica.

questions.question: Arrange the words to describe snow:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: 'Snow is cold and white.' It falls during winter.

questions.question: When it is winter in the northern part of the world, it is summer in the _______ part.
questions.explanation: The Southern hemisphere has summer when the Northern hemisphere has winter.

questions.question: In winter at the North Pole, there is no sun, so it is _______ all day.
questions.explanation: Without the sun, it remains dark all day long near the North Pole in winter.

questions.question: Arrange the words to show what some bears do:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: 'In winter some bears hibernate.' This helps them survive the cold.

questions.question: Plants hibernate in the winter just like bears do.
questions.explanation: False. Only animals can hibernate. Plants stop growing or die, but they do not hibernate.

questions.question: Which of these sentences is correct?
options: The North Pole is located at the equator.
In winter, the sun never sets at the North Pole.
The North Pole has dark, sunless days in winter.
Geese travel to the North Pole in winter.
questions.explanation: The North Pole is at the top of Earth. It has dark days in winter because it tilts away from the sun.
